⇒ Relative Speed = 21 + 24 = 45 km/hr

⇒ Total Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 45 × 1.2

⇒ Distance = 54 km

∴ The correct answer is 54 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference between their speeds: Srel = |S1 − S2|.

Conversion of Units

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Time of Meeting

Time taken to meet = Initial distance between objects ÷ Relative Speed.

questions.question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 km/h and including stoppages, it is 45 km/h. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?
questions.questionHtml: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 km/h and including stoppages, it is 45 km/h. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Stoppage time per hour = (Difference in speeds ÷ Speed excluding stoppages) × 60 minutes

Difference in speeds = 60 km/h − 45 km/h = 15 km/h

Stoppage time = (15 ÷ 60) × 60 minutes

Stoppage time = 15 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of bus (Excluding stoppages) = 60 km/h

Speed of bus (Including stoppages) = 45 km/h

Formula Used:

Stoppage time per hour = (Distance lost due to stoppage ÷ Original speed) × 60

Calculations:

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour without stoppage = 60 km

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour with stoppage = 45 km

⇒ Distance not covered due to stoppage = 60 km − 45 km = 15 km

⇒ Time taken to cover this 15 km at 60 km/h = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time = 15 ÷ 60 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = (15 ÷ 60) × 60

⇒ Time = 15 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.

Additional Information

General Stoppage Rule

Rest time per hour = (Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed. Multiply by 60 to get the value in minutes.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. Including stoppages reduces the average speed because the total time increases while the distance remains the same.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert hours to minutes, multiply by 60.

questions.question: If in 3 years, at simple interest, the principal increases by 15%. What will be the approximate compound interest earned (in Rs lakhs) on Rs. 15 lakhs in 3 years at the same rate?
questions.questionHtml: If in 3 years, at simple interest, the principal increases by 15%. What will be the approximate compound interest earned (in Rs lakhs) on Rs. 15 lakhs in 3 years at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Annual Simple Interest Rate = 15% ÷ 3 years = 5% p.a.

Effective Compound Interest rate for 3 years at 5% = 15.7625%.

CI = 15 lakhs × 15.7625% = 2.364375 lakhs.

Approximate value = ₹2.36 lakhs.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2.36 lakhs.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = ₹15 lakhs, Time (T) = 3 years, SI increase = 15%.

Formula used: CI = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1]

⇒ Simple Interest Rate (R) = 15% ÷ 3 = 5% p.a.

⇒ Amount (A) = 15 × (1 + 5/100)3

⇒ A = 15 × (1.05)3

⇒ A = 15 × 1.157625 = 17.364375 lakhs.

⇒ CI = Amount − Principal = 17.364375 − 15

⇒ CI = 2.364375 lakhs ≈ ₹2.36 lakhs.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2.36 lakhs.

Additional Information

Successive Rate Formula

For two years, effective CI rate is [x + y + (xy/100)]%. For 5%, it is 5 + 5 + 0.25 = 10.25%.

CI-SI Difference for 3 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is given by P(R/100)2 × (3 + R/100).

3-Year Ratio Method

Compound Interest for 3 years can be calculated using the ratio 3 : 3 : 1 applied to interests on interests.

questions.question: If the amount received at the end of 2nd and 3rd year at compound Interest on a certain Principal is Rs. 9,600 and Rs. 10,272 respectively, what is the rate of interest (in %)?
questions.questionHtml: If the amount received at the end of 2nd and 3rd year at compound Interest on a certain Principal is Rs. 9,600 and Rs. 10,272 respectively, what is the rate of interest (in %)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest earned in the 3rd year = ₹10,272 − ₹9,600 = ₹672.

In compound interest, the amount at the end of the 2nd year acts as the principal for the 3rd year.

Rate % = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

Rate % = (672 ÷ 9,600) × 100 = 7%

∴ The correct answer is 7%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 2 years (A2) = ₹9,600

Amount after 3 years (A3) = ₹10,272

Formula Used:

A = P(1 + R/100)n

For consecutive years: An+1 = An(1 + R/100)

Calculations:

⇒ A3 = A2 × (1 + R/100)

⇒ 10,272 = 9,600 × (1 + R/100)

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 10,272 ÷ 9,600

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 1.07

⇒ R/100 = 1.07 − 1

⇒ R/100 = 0.07

⇒ R = 7

∴ The correct answer is 7%.

Additional Information

Successive Year Interest

In compound interest, the difference between the amounts of two consecutive years is the interest on the amount of the preceding year. R = [(An+1 − An) ÷ An] × 100.

Compound Interest Formula

The general formula for amount is A = P(1 + R/100)n, where P is principal, R is rate per annum, and n is time in years.

SI vs CI for 2 Years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given by D = P × (R/100)2.

questions.question: A invested an amount of x rupees in a bank at compound interest for 2 years which gave 5% interest in year 1 and 6% interest in year 2. The amount received after 2 years is Rs 24,486. What is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: A invested an amount of x rupees in a bank at compound interest for 2 years which gave 5% interest in year 1 and 6% interest in year 2. The amount received after 2 years is Rs 24,486. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net effective interest rate for 2 years = 5 + 6 + (5 × 6) ÷ 100 = 11.3%

Total amount percentage = 100% (Principal) + 11.3% (Interest) = 111.3%

Given: 111.3% of x = Rs 24,486

Value of x = 24,486 ÷ 1.113

Value of x = 22,000

∴ The correct answer is Rs 22000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal = Rs x

Rate for year 1 (R1) = 5%

Rate for year 2 (R2) = 6%

Amount (A) after 2 years = Rs 24,486

Formula Used:

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R1/100) × (1 + R2/100)

Calculations:

⇒ 24,486 = x × (1 + 5/100) × (1 + 6/100)

⇒ 24,486 = x × (105/100) × (106/100)

⇒ 24,486 = x × (21/20) × (53/50)

⇒ 24,486 = x × (1113/1000)

⇒ x = (24,486 × 1000) ÷ 1113

⇒ x = 22 × 1000

⇒ x = 22,000

∴ The correct answer is Rs 22000.

Additional Information

Net Effective Rate for Successive Years

For two successive years with interest rates r1% and r2%, the combined effective interest rate is (r1 + r2 + r1r2/100)%.

General Amount Formula for CI

When interest rates are different for each year, Amount = P × (1 + r1/100) × (1 + r2/100) × ... × (1 + rn/100).

Compound Interest (CI)

Compound Interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods, given by CI = Amount − Principal.

questions.question: What is the difference (in Rs) between compound interest earned in 1 year on a sum of Rs. 10,000 at 40% per annum compounded quarterly and annually?
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference (in Rs) between compound interest earned in 1 year on a sum of Rs. 10,000 at 40% per annum compounded quarterly and annually?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Effective rate for annual compounding = 40%

For quarterly compounding: Rate = 40% ÷ 4 = 10% and Time = 4 quarters

Effective rate for 4 periods of 10% = 46.41% (Using successive percentage formula)

Difference in interest = (46.41% − 40%) of ₹10,000 = 6.41% of 10,000

Difference = 0.0641 × 10,000 = ₹641

∴ The correct answer is ₹641.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = ₹10,000, Rate (R) = 40% p.a., Time (T) = 1 year.

Formula Used: Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)n; CI = A − P

Case 1: Compounded Annually

⇒ CI1 = P × R × T / 100 = 10,000 × 40 × 1 / 100

⇒ CI1 = ₹4,000

Case 2: Compounded Quarterly

⇒ Quarterly Rate (r) = 40 ÷ 4 = 10% per quarter

⇒ Number of quarters (n) = 1 × 4 = 4

⇒ Amount (A) = 10,000 × (1 + 10/100)4

⇒ A = 10,000 × (1.1)4 = 10,000 × 1.4641

⇒ A = ₹14,641

⇒ CI2 = 14,641 − 10,000 = ₹4,641

Difference in CI:

⇒ Difference = CI2 − CI1 = 4,641 − 4,000

⇒ Difference = ₹641

∴ The correct answer is ₹641.

Additional Information

Effective Interest Rate

The effective annual rate increases with the frequency of compounding. For n periods at rate r, the effective rate is [(1 + r/100)n − 1] × 100%.

Compounding Frequency Rules

Half-yearly: Rate = R/2, Time = 2T. Quarterly: Rate = R/4, Time = 4T. Monthly: Rate = R/12, Time = 12T.

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the net change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%. This can be used iteratively for compound interest.

questions.question: Giving two successive discounts of 40% is equal to giving one discount of ________%.
questions.questionHtml: Giving two successive discounts of 40% is equal to giving one discount of ________%.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the single equivalent discount is (x + y − xy/100)%.

Here, x = 40% and y = 40%.

Equivalent Discount = (40 + 40 − (40 × 40)/100)%

Equivalent Discount = (80 − 1600/100)% = (80 − 16)% = 64%

∴ The correct answer is 64%.

Alternate Method

Given:

First Discount (D1) = 40%

Second Discount (D2) = 40%

Formula Used:

Final Price = Marked Price × (1 − D1/100) × (1 − D2/100)

Single Discount % = [(Marked Price − Final Price) / Marked Price] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) = ₹100

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 100 − (40% of 100) = 100 − 40 = ₹60

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 60 − (40% of 60) = 60 − 24 = ₹36

⇒ Total Discount = MP − Final Selling Price = 100 − 36 = 64

⇒ Equivalent Discount Percentage = (64 / 100) × 100 = 64%

∴ The correct answer is 64%.

Additional Information

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective discount is (a + b − ab/100)%. This is always less than the sum of individual discounts.

Three Successive Discounts

For three discounts a%, b%, and c%, the net discount is [1 − (1 − a/100)(1 − b/100)(1 − c/100)] × 100%. Alternatively, apply the two-discount formula twice.

Fraction Method for Discounts

Convert percentage to fractions (e.g., 40% = 2/5). If the initial value is 5, after a 2/5 discount, the value becomes 3. Successive discounts are calculated by multiplying the ratios: (3/5) × (3/5) = 9/25. Discount = (25 − 9)/25 = 16/25 = 64%.

questions.question: If a website is selling smartphone at Rs. 18,000 which is marked at Rs. 25,000, then what is the discount (in %) at which the smartphone is being sold?
questions.questionHtml: If a website is selling smartphone at Rs. 18,000 which is marked at Rs. 25,000, then what is the discount (in %) at which the smartphone is being sold?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of MP : SP = 25,000 : 18,000 = 25 : 18

Discount units = 25 − 18 = 7 units

Discount % = (7 ÷ 25) × 100

Discount % = 7 × 4 = 28%

∴ The correct answer is 28%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marked Price (MP) = ₹25,000

Selling Price (SP) = ₹18,000

Formula Used:

Discount = MP − SP

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Discount = 25,000 − 18,000

⇒ Discount = ₹7,000

⇒ Discount % = (7,000 ÷ 25,000) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (7 ÷ 25) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 28%

∴ The correct answer is 28%.

Additional Information

Marked Price (MP)

It is also known as the List Price or Tag Price. It is the price printed on the label of an item.

Selling Price (SP)

The actual price at which a product is sold after deducting the discount from the Marked Price. SP = MP − Discount.

Relation between CP and MP

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%). This is useful for finding the markup percentage.

questions.question: If, on an item, there is 12% discount on the marked price of Rs. 10,000 but the item is sold at Rs. 8,360 only then what additional discount (in %) did the customer get?
questions.questionHtml: If, on an item, there is 12% discount on the marked price of Rs. 10,000 but the item is sold at Rs. 8,360 only then what additional discount (in %) did the customer get?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Marked Price (MP) = ₹10,000

Price after first 12% discount = 88% of 10,000 = ₹8,800

Final Selling Price (SP) = ₹8,360

Additional discount amount = 8,800 − 8,360 = ₹440

Additional discount % = (440 ÷ 8,800) × 100 = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marked Price (MP) = ₹10,000

First discount (d1) = 12%

Final Selling Price (SP) = ₹8,360

Formula Used:

Selling Price = MP × (100 − d1)/100 × (100 − d2)/100

Calculations:

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 10,000 × (100 − 12) ÷ 100

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 10,000 × 0.88 = ₹8,800

⇒ Let additional discount be x%.

⇒ 8,360 = 8,800 × (100 − x) ÷ 100

⇒ 8,360 ÷ 88 = 100 − x

⇒ 95 = 100 − x

⇒ x = 100 − 95

⇒ x = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Additional Information

Successive Discount Formula

If two successive discounts are a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is given by (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Marked Price (MP) is the tag price, and Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount. Discount is always calculated on the MP unless stated otherwise.

Effective Discount Rate

The effective discount rate can be calculated as [(Initial MP − Final SP) ÷ Initial MP] × 100.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks up his wares by 125% and offers 25% discount. What will be the selling price if the cost price (in Rs) is Rs. 640?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marks up his wares by 125% and offers 25% discount. What will be the selling price if the cost price (in Rs) is Rs. 640?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Markup factor = 100% + 125% = 225% = 9/4

Discount factor = 100% − 25% = 75% = 3/4

Selling Price = CP × Markup Factor × Discount Factor

SP = 640 × (9/4) × (3/4) = 640 × 27/16 = 40 × 27 = 1080

∴ The correct answer is ₹1080.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) = ₹640

Markup Percentage = 125%

Discount Percentage = 25%

Formula Used:

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (100 + Markup%)/100

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

Calculations:

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 640 + (125% of 640)

⇒ MP = 640 + (1.25 × 640) = 640 + 800

⇒ MP = ₹1440

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − (Discount% of MP)

⇒ SP = 1440 − (25% of 1440)

⇒ SP = 1440 − (1/4 × 1440)

⇒ SP = 1440 − 360 = ₹1080

∴ The correct answer is ₹1080.

Additional Information

Effective Profit/Loss Percentage

The net profit or loss percentage can be calculated using the successive percentage formula: Net Change = M + D + (M × D)/100, where M is markup percentage (positive) and D is discount percentage (negative).

Relation between CP and MP

A very useful ratio for exams is CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%). This directly relates the costs when profit and discount are known.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d1 and d2 are given, the single equivalent discount is (d1 + d2 − d1d2/100)%.

questions.question: Priya's marks in History and Geography are in the ratio 5 : 7. If she got 14 marks more in Geography than in History, what are her History marks?
questions.questionHtml: Priya's marks in History and Geography are in the ratio 5 : 7. If she got 14 marks more in Geography than in History, what are her History marks?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of History : Geography = 5 : 7

Difference in ratio units = 7 − 5 = 2 units

Given difference in marks = 14

⇒ 2 units = 14 marks

⇒ 1 unit = 7 marks

History marks = 5 units = 5 × 7 = 35 marks

∴ The correct answer is 35 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of History marks to Geography marks = 5 : 7

Geography marks − History marks = 14

Let History marks be 5x and Geography marks be 7x.

According to the question:

⇒ 7x − 5x = 14

⇒ 2x = 14

⇒ x = 14 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 7

History marks = 5x

⇒ History marks = 5 × 7

⇒ History marks = 35

∴ The correct answer is 35 marks.

Additional Information

Ratio and Proportion Basics

If two quantities are in the ratio a : b, they can be represented as ax and bx, where x is the constant of proportionality.

Difference Property

When the difference between two quantities is given, the value of one unit in the ratio is equal to the Absolute Difference ÷ Difference in Ratio Parts.

Percentage Conversion

To find what percentage one part of a ratio is of the total: [Part / (a+b)] × 100.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of Rahul and his sister is 3 : 4. 10 years ago, the ratio of their ages was 13 : 19. What is Rahul's present age (in years)?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of present ages of Rahul and his sister is 3 : 4. 10 years ago, the ratio of their ages was 13 : 19. What is Rahul's present age (in years)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Make the difference between ratios equal: Present ratio (3:4, diff = 1) and Past ratio (13:19, diff = 6).

Multiply Present ratio by 6 → 18 : 24. Past ratio remains 13 : 19.

Difference in units = 18 − 13 = 5 units. Given time difference = 10 years.

5 units = 10 years ⇒ 1 unit = 2 years.

Rahul's present age = 18 units = 18 × 2 = 36 years.

∴ The correct answer is 36 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Present ratio of Rahul and Sister = 3 : 4

Ratio 10 years ago = 13 : 19

Formula Used:

Age Ratio Equation: (Age1 − n) ÷ (Age2 − n) = New Ratio

Calculations:

Let the present ages of Rahul and his sister be 3x and 4x respectively.

⇒ (3x − 10) ÷ (4x − 10) = 13 ÷ 19

⇒ 19 × (3x − 10) = 13 × (4x − 10)

⇒ 57x − 190 = 52x − 130

⇒ 57x − 52x = 190 − 130

⇒ 5x = 60

⇒ x = 12

⇒ Rahul's present age = 3x = 3 × 12 = 36 years.

∴ The correct answer is 36 years.

Additional Information

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains the same regardless of how many years pass. This property is used to equalize ratio differences.

Ratio Balancing Method

If ratio at T1 is a:b and at T2 is c:d, and time gap is same for both, multiply ratios by the difference of the other ratio (b−a) and (d−c) to balance them.

Future Age Calculation

To find age after 'n' years, add 'n' to the present age. Ratio changes accordingly but absolute difference stays constant.

questions.question: What is the third proportional to 9 and 15?
questions.questionHtml: What is the third proportional to 9 and 15?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The third proportional to two numbers a and b is calculated as b2 ÷ a.

Here, a = 9 and b = 15.

Third proportional = (15 × 15) ÷ 9

Third proportional = 225 ÷ 9 = 25.

∴ The correct answer is 25.

Alternate Method

Given: First number (a) = 9, Second number (b) = 15.

Formula: If a, b, and c are in continued proportion, then a : b :: b : c, where c is the third proportional.

⇒ 9 : 15 :: 15 : x

⇒ 9 ÷ 15 = 15 ÷ x

⇒ 9 × x = 15 × 15

⇒ 9x = 225

⇒ x = 225 ÷ 9

⇒ x = 25

∴ The correct answer is 25.

Additional Information

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(a × b).

Fourth Proportional

If a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then the fourth proportional d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Continued Proportion

Three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion if a/b = b/c, which implies b2 = ac.

questions.question: According to the will, the wealth of Rs. 11,50,000 was to be divided between the son and the daughter in the ratio 2/3 : 5/4. How much share did the son get (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions.questionHtml: According to the will, the wealth of Rs. 11,50,000 was to be divided between the son and the daughter in the ratio 2/3 : 5/4. How much share did the son get (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Simplified Ratio (Son : Daughter) = (2/3 × 12) : (5/4 × 12) = 8 : 15.

Total units = 8 + 15 = 23 units.

23 units = 11.5 lakhs ⇒ 1 unit = 0.5 lakhs.

Son's share = 8 units × 0.5 lakhs = 4 lakhs.

∴ The correct answer is 4 lakhs.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total wealth = ₹11,50,000

Ratio of wealth (Son : Daughter) = 2/3 : 5/4

Formula Used:

Share of a person = (Individual ratio ÷ Sum of ratios) × Total Value

Calculations:

⇒ Ratio = 2/3 : 5/4

⇒ Multiply both terms by LCM of 3 and 4, which is 12.

⇒ New Ratio = (2/3 × 12) : (5/4 × 12) = 8 : 15

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 8 + 15 = 23

⇒ Total wealth in lakhs = 11,50,000 ÷ 1,00,000 = 11.5 lakhs

⇒ Value of 23 parts = 11.5 lakhs

⇒ Value of 1 part = 11.5 ÷ 23 = 0.5 lakhs

⇒ Son's share = 8 parts × 0.5 lakhs = 4 lakhs

∴ The correct answer is 4 lakhs.

Additional Information

Simplifying Fractional Ratios

To convert a fractional ratio a/b : c/d into a linear ratio, multiply both terms by the LCM of denominators b and d, or simply cross-multiply to get (a×d) : (b×c).

Proportional Division

If a quantity X is divided in the ratio a : b, then the shares are [a/(a+b)] × X and [b/(a+b)] × X respectively.

Unit Conversion

1 Lakh = 1,00,000. To convert a value into lakhs, divide the total amount by 1,00,000.

questions.question: If Rs 7,800 is to be divided between A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4, then how much share will B get (in Rs)?
questions.questionHtml: If Rs 7,800 is to be divided between A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4, then how much share will B get (in Rs)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Convert fraction ratio to integer ratio by multiplying with LCM(2, 3, 4) = 12.

Ratio A : B : C = (1/2 × 12) : (1/3 × 12) : (1/4 × 12) = 6 : 4 : 3.

Total units = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13 units.

Total Amount → 13 units = ₹7,800 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹600.

B's share = 4 units = 4 × ₹600 = ₹2,400.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2400.

Alternate Method

Given: Total amount = ₹7,800 | Ratio A : B : C = 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4

Formula: Share of X = (Ratio of X ÷ Sum of Ratios) × Total Amount

Step 1: Simplify the ratio of A, B, and C.

⇒ LCM of 2, 3, 4 is 12.

⇒ A = 1/2 × 12 = 6 parts

⇒ B = 1/3 × 12 = 4 parts

⇒ C = 1/4 × 12 = 3 parts

Step 2: Calculate the total parts.

⇒ Total parts = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13 parts.

Step 3: Calculate B's share.

⇒ B's share = (4 / 13) × 7,800

⇒ B's share = 4 × (7800 ÷ 13)

⇒ B's share = 4 × 600

⇒ B's share = ₹2,400

∴ The correct answer is ₹2400.

Additional Information

Ratio Simplification

To convert a fractional ratio a/b : c/d to an integer ratio, multiply both terms by the LCM of denominators b and d.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios (a : b) and (c : d) is (ac : bd), calculated by multiplying the respective antecedents and consequents.

Invertendo and Alternendo

If a/b = c/d, then b/a = d/c (Invertendo) and a/c = b/d (Alternendo). These are useful properties for solving proportion-based questions.

questions.question: Bunty had candies and chewing gums in his sweet box in the ratio 7 : 13. After he has eaten 8 candies and 11 chewing gums the ratio became 1 : 2. How many candies does he have now?
questions.questionHtml: Bunty had candies and chewing gums in his sweet box in the ratio 7 : 13. After he has eaten 8 candies and 11 chewing gums the ratio became 1 : 2. How many candies does he have now?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial Ratio of candies and gums = 7 : 13

Final Ratio after eating 8 candies and 11 gums = 1 : 2

Apply Cross-Product: (7 × 2 − 13 × 1) units = |(8 × 2) − (11 × 1)|

1 unit = |16 − 11| = 5

Initial candies = 7 units = 7 × 5 = 35. Candies remaining = 35 − 8 = 27.

∴ The correct answer is 27.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Ratio (Candies : Gums) = 7 : 13

Items eaten: Candies = 8, Chewing gums = 11

New Ratio = 1 : 2

Formula Used:

Let the initial counts be 7x and 13x. (Initial − Eaten) / (Initial − Eaten) = New Ratio

Calculations:

⇒ (7x − 8) / (13x − 11) = 1 / 2

⇒ 2 × (7x − 8) = 1 × (13x − 11)

⇒ 14x − 16 = 13x − 11

⇒ 14x − 13x = 16 − 11

⇒ x = 5

⇒ Number of candies initially = 7 × 5 = 35

⇒ Number of candies Bunty has now = 35 − 8 = 27

∴ The correct answer is 27.

Additional Information

Cross-Product Method for Ratios

When values are added or subtracted from the terms of a ratio to get a new ratio, 1 unit = |(R2 term1 × Change2) − (R2 term2 × Change1)| ÷ |Difference of cross products of Ratios|.

Ratio and Proportion Basics

If a : b is the ratio, always represent the actual values as ax and bx. Proportions occur when a/b = c/d, allowing for cross-multiplication (ad = bc).

Unitary Method in Ratios

Finding the value of 'x' or '1 unit' allows for the direct calculation of any part of the ratio at any point in time.

questions.question: If x – 4y = 0 and x + 2y = 24, then what is the value of (2x + 3y) / (2x – 3y)?
questions.questionHtml: If x – 4y = 0 and x + 2y = 24, then what is the value of (2x + 3y) / (2x – 3y)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

From x − 4y = 0, we get x = 4y or x : y = 4 : 1.

Substitute x = 4 and y = 1 in the second equation: 4 + 2(1) = 6 units.

Given 6 units = 24 → 1 unit = 4. Thus x = 16 and y = 4.

Required Ratio = (2 × 16 + 3 × 4) ÷ (2 × 16 − 3 × 4) = 44 ÷ 20.

Simplifying 44/20 gives 11/5.

∴ The correct answer is 11/5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation 1: x − 4y = 0

Equation 2: x + 2y = 24

Formula Used:

Substitution method for linear equations in two variables.

Calculations:

⇒ From Equation 1: x = 4y

⇒ Substitute x = 4y in Equation 2:

⇒ 4y + 2y = 24

⇒ 6y = 24

⇒ y = 24 ÷ 6 = 4

⇒ Now, x = 4 × 4 = 16

⇒ Substitute values of x and y in (2x + 3y) ÷ (2x − 3y):

⇒ (2 × 16 + 3 × 4) ÷ (2 × 16 − 3 × 4)

⇒ (32 + 12) ÷ (32 − 12)

⇒ 44 ÷ 20

⇒ 11/5

∴ The correct answer is 11/5.

Additional Information

Substitution Method

It involves expressing one variable in terms of the other from one equation and substituting it into the second equation to solve for the variables.

Ratio Simplification

A ratio a/b is simplified by dividing both terms by their Highest Common Factor (HCF). In this case, HCF of 44 and 20 is 4, so 44/20 = 11/5.

Nature of Linear Equations

Two linear equations in two variables (x and y) represent two lines. Their intersection point gives the unique solution for x and y.

questions.question: If (x/a) + (y/b) = 3 and (x/b) – (y/a) = 9, then what is the value of x/y?
questions.questionHtml: If (x/a) + (y/b) = 3 and (x/b) – (y/a) = 9, then what is the value of x/y?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Scale the first equation by 3 to match the constant 9 of the second equation.

Equate the resulting expressions: ax − by = 3(bx + ay).

Rearrange to group terms: ax − 3bx = 3ay + by.

Factor out variables: x(a − 3b) = y(3a + b).

∴ The correct answer is (b + 3a) / (a − 3b).

Alternate Method

Given equations:

(x/a) + (y/b) = 3 ... (i)

(x/b) − (y/a) = 9 ... (ii)

Formula used: Algebraic manipulation of linear equations.

⇒ From equation (i): (xb + ya) / ab = 3 ⇒ xb + ya = 3ab

⇒ From equation (ii): (xa − yb) / ab = 9 ⇒ xa − yb = 9ab

⇒ To eliminate the constant ab, express 9ab as 3 × (3ab):

⇒ xa − yb = 3(xb + ya)

⇒ xa − yb = 3xb + 3ya

⇒ Grouping x terms on the left and y terms on the right:

⇒ xa − 3xb = 3ya + yb

⇒ x(a − 3b) = y(3a + b)

⇒ x/y = (3a + b) / (a − 3b)

⇒ Rearranging the numerator: x/y = (b + 3a) / (a − 3b)

∴ The correct answer is (b + 3a) / (a − 3b).

Additional Information

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Equations of the form ax + by = c, where a, b, and c are constants. They can be solved using substitution, elimination, or cross-multiplication.

Ratio and Proportion

A ratio x/y compares two quantities. In algebraic expressions, it is found by isolating the variables on opposite sides of the equation.

Cross-Multiplication Method

For a system a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0, the variables can be solved using the ratio x / (b1c2 − b2c1) = y / (c1a2 − c2a1).

questions.question: In the given figure, OX, OY and OZ are the perpendicular side bisectors of the three sides of the triangle. If ∠QPR = 65° and ∠PQR = 60°, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠QOR + ∠POR?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, OX, OY and OZ are the perpendicular side bisectors of the three sides of the triangle. If ∠QPR = 65° and ∠PQR = 60°, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠QOR + ∠POR?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

OX, OY, and OZ are perpendicular side bisectors, so O is the circumcenter.

Angle at the circumcenter is twice the angle at the opposite vertex.

∠QOR = 2 × ∠QPR = 2 × 65° = 130°.

∠POR = 2 × ∠PQR = 2 × 60° = 120°.

∠QOR + ∠POR = 130° + 120° = 250°.

∴ The correct answer is 250°.

Alternate Method

Given:

∠QPR = 65° and ∠PQR = 60°

OX, OY, OZ are perpendicular side bisectors of ΔPQR.

Formula Used:

In a triangle, the intersection of perpendicular side bisectors is the circumcenter (O).

Angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended at the circumference.

∠Central = 2 × ∠Inscribed

Calculations:

⇒ O is the circumcenter of ΔPQR.

⇒ ∠QOR = 2 × ∠QPR

⇒ ∠QOR = 2 × 65° = 130°

⇒ ∠POR = 2 × ∠PQR

⇒ ∠POR = 2 × 60° = 120°

⇒ Required Sum = ∠QOR + ∠POR

⇒ Required Sum = 130° + 120° = 250°

∴ The correct answer is 250°.

Additional Information

Circumcenter Properties

The circumcenter (O) is the center of the circle passing through all vertices. The circumradius R = abc / 4A, where a, b, c are sides and A is the area.

Incenter Angle Property

If I is the incenter of ΔABC, then ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A/2.

Orthocenter Angle Property

If H is the orthocenter (intersection of altitudes), then ∠BHC = 180° − ∠A.

Centroid Property

The centroid (G) divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex.

questions.question: In a triangle PQR, ∠PQR = 90°, PQ = 10 cm and PR = 26 cm, then what is the value (in cm) of inradius of incircle?
questions.questionHtml: In a triangle PQR, ∠PQR = 90°, PQ = 10 cm and PR = 26 cm, then what is the value (in cm) of inradius of incircle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Triangle PQR is a right-angled triangle at Q (∠Q = 90°).

Given PQ = 10 cm and PR = 26 cm (Hypotenuse).

Using Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13) × 2 → (10, 24, 26). Thus, QR = 24 cm.

Inradius (r) of a right triangle = (Base + Perpendicular − Hypotenuse) ÷ 2

r = (10 + 24 − 26) ÷ 2 = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Perpendicular (PQ) = 10 cm

Hypotenuse (PR) = 26 cm

Formula Used:

Third side (QR) = √(PR2 − PQ2)

Inradius (r) = Area ÷ Semi-perimeter (s)

Calculations:

⇒ QR = √(262 − 102)

⇒ QR = √(676 − 100) = √576 = 24 cm

⇒ Area of ΔPQR = 1/2 × Base × Height

⇒ Area = 0.5 × 24 × 10 = 120 cm2

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = (10 + 24 + 26) ÷ 2 = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm

⇒ Inradius (r) = Area ÷ s = 120 ÷ 30

⇒ r = 4 cm

∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.

Additional Information

Circumradius of Right Triangle

The circumradius (R) of a right-angled triangle is equal to half of its hypotenuse: R = Hypotenuse ÷ 2.

General Inradius Formula

For any triangle, the inradius r is given by Area (A) ÷ Semi-perimeter (s), where s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25) help in solving right triangle problems faster.

questions.question: In the given figure, if QR/XY = 14/9 and PY = 18 cm, then what is the value (in cm) of PQ?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, if QR/XY = 14/9 and PY = 18 cm, then what is the value (in cm) of PQ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In triangle PQR, since XY ∥ QR, then ▵PXY ∼ ▵PQR.

Ratio of corresponding sides: PY : PQ = XY : QR

Given QR/XY = 14/9 ⇒ XY/QR = 9/14

So, PY : PQ = 9 : 14

9 units = 18 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 2 cm

PQ = 14 units = 14 × 2 = 28 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: QR/XY = 14/9, PY = 18 cm, and XY ∥ QR.

Formula Used: Basic Proportionality Theorem / Similarity of Triangles.

In ▵PQR and ▵PYX:

∠P = ∠P (Common angle)

∠PYX = ∠PQR (Corresponding angles as XY ∥ QR)

∴ ▵PXY ∼ ▵PQR (By AA similarity)

⇒ PY / PQ = XY / QR

⇒ 18 / PQ = 9 / 14

⇒ 9 × PQ = 18 × 14

⇒ PQ = (18 × 14) ÷ 9

⇒ PQ = 2 × 14

⇒ PQ = 28 cm

∴ The correct answer is 28 cm.

Additional Information

Thales Theorem (BPT)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio: PY/YQ = PX/XR.

Similarity Property

For similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(▵PXY) / Area(▵PQR) = (XY/QR)2.

AA Similarity Criterion

If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar, and their sides are proportional.

questions.question: In a triangle PQR, PX, QY and RZ be altitudes intersecting at O. If PO = 6 cm, PX = 8 cm and QO = 4 cm, then what is the value (in cm) of QY?
questions.questionHtml: In a triangle PQR, PX, QY and RZ be altitudes intersecting at O. If PO = 6 cm, PX = 8 cm and QO = 4 cm, then what is the value (in cm) of QY?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For orthocenter O and altitudes PX, QY of ΔPQR, the property of segments is: PO × OX = QO × OY.

Given PX = 8 cm and PO = 6 cm ⇒ OX = 8 − 6 = 2 cm.

Applying the formula: 6 × 2 = 4 × OY ⇒ 12 = 4 × OY ⇒ OY = 3 cm.

Total length of altitude QY = QO + OY = 4 + 3 = 7 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: PO = 6 cm, PX = 8 cm, QO = 4 cm.

Formula: In any triangle, the product of the segments of the altitudes from the orthocenter to the vertices and the sides is constant: PO × OX = QO × OY = RO × OZ.

In ΔPQR, PX and QY are altitudes intersecting at orthocenter O.

⇒ Altitude PX = PO + OX

⇒ 8 = 6 + OX

⇒ OX = 8 − 6 = 2 cm

Since ∠PYO = ∠QXO = 90° and ∠POY = ∠QOX (vertically opposite angles),

ΔPOY ∼ ΔQOX (by AA similarity criteria)

⇒ PO / QO = OY / OX

⇒ 6 / 4 = OY / 2

⇒ OY = (6 × 2) / 4

⇒ OY = 12 / 4 = 3 cm

Now, altitude QY = QO + OY

⇒ QY = 4 + 3 = 7 cm

∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.

Additional Information

Orthocenter Angle Property

The angle formed by any two sides at the orthocenter is supplementary to the opposite interior angle of the triangle: ∠QOR = 180° − ∠P.

Concyclic Points

In ΔPQR with altitudes PX and QY, the points P, Q, X, and Y are concyclic because ∠PYQ = ∠PXQ = 90°, both subtending the same segment PQ.

Location of Orthocenter

The orthocenter lies inside an acute-angled triangle, outside an obtuse-angled triangle, and at the vertex of the right angle in a right-angled triangle.

questions.question: A line cuts two concentric circles. The length of the chords formed by that line on the two circles are 4 cm and 16 cm. What is the difference (in cm 2 ) in squares of radii of two circles?
questions.questionHtml: A line cuts two concentric circles. The length of the chords formed by that line on the two circles are 4 cm and 16 cm. What is the difference (in cm<sup>2</sup>) in squares of radii of two circles?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two concentric circles, if a line forms chords of lengths L1 and L2, then the difference in squares of their radii is given by:

Difference = (L1/2)2 − (L2/2)2

Here, L1 = 16 cm and L2 = 4 cm.

R2 − r2 = (16/2)2 − (4/2)2 = 82 − 22

R2 − r2 = 64 − 4 = 60 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 60 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of chord in outer circle (AB) = 16 cm

Length of chord in inner circle (CD) = 4 cm

Let R be the radius of the outer circle and r be the radius of the inner circle.

Let OM = d be the perpendicular distance from center O to the line.

The perpendicular from the center bisects the chord.

⇒ In outer circle, AM = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm

⇒ In inner circle, CM = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm

Using Pythagoras theorem in ▵OMA:

⇒ R2 = d2 + AM2

⇒ R2 = d2 + 82 = d2 + 64

Using Pythagoras theorem in ▵OMC:

⇒ r2 = d2 + CM2

⇒ r2 = d2 + 22 = d2 + 4

Subtracting the two equations:

⇒ R2 − r2 = (d2 + 64) − (d2 + 4)

⇒ R2 − r2 = 64 − 4 = 60 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 60 cm2.

Additional Information

Perpendicular Bisector Property

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Area of Annulus

The area of the ring (annulus) formed between two concentric circles is π(R2 − r2). In this problem, Area = 60π cm2.

Chord Relations

For two chords of different circles sharing the same center and the same line, the distance between the endpoints on the same side is constant: AC = BD = (L1 − L2)/2.

questions.question: In the given figure, a circle touches the sides of a quadrilateral PQRS. The radius of the circle is 9 cm. ∠RSP = ∠SRQ = 60° and ∠PQR = ∠QPS = 120°. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the quadrilateral?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, a circle touches the sides of a quadrilateral PQRS. The radius of the circle is 9 cm. ∠RSP = ∠SRQ = 60° and ∠PQR = ∠QPS = 120°. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the quadrilateral?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For an isosceles trapezoid circumscribing a circle, the perimeter is calculated as 4 × (h ÷ sin θ), where h is the diameter and θ is the base angle.

Diameter (h) = 2 × Radius = 2 × 9 = 18 cm.

Side PS = h ÷ sin 60° = 18 ÷ (√3/2) = 36/√3 = 12√3 cm.

Perimeter = 4 × Side PS = 4 × 12√3 = 48√3 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 48√3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: Radius of circle (r) = 9 cm, ∠RSP = ∠SRQ = 60°, ∠PQR = ∠QPS = 120°.

Formula Used: Diameter of inscribed circle = Height of the trapezoid; For a tangential quadrilateral, Sum of opposite sides is equal (PQ + RS = PS + QR).

⇒ Height of the quadrilateral (h) = 2 × Radius = 2 × 9 = 18 cm.

⇒ In right-angled triangle formed by height from P to side SR, sin 60° = Height / PS.

⇒ √3 / 2 = 18 / PS.

⇒ PS = (18 × 2) / √3 = 36 / √3 = 12√3 cm.

⇒ Due to symmetry (isosceles trapezoid), QR = PS = 12√3 cm.

⇒ According to Pitot's Theorem for tangential quadrilaterals: PQ + RS = PS + QR.

⇒ Total Perimeter = (PQ + RS) + (PS + QR) = 2 × (PS + QR).

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (12√3 + 12√3) = 2 × 24√3 = 48√3 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 48√3 cm.

Additional Information

Pitot Theorem

In any quadrilateral circumscribed about a circle, the sum of the lengths of opposite sides is equal: a + c = b + d.

Isosceles Trapezoid Inscribed Circle

A trapezoid can have an inscribed circle only if the sum of its parallel sides equals the sum of its non-parallel sides. The height is always equal to the diameter (2r).

Area of Tangential Quadrilateral

The area (A) of a quadrilateral that has an incircle is given by A = r × s, where r is the inradius and s is the semi-perimeter.

questions.question: In the given figure, from the point P two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O and radius 5 cm. From the point O, OC and OD are drawn parallel to PA and PB respectively. If the length of the chord AB is 5 cm, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠COD?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, from the point P two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O and radius 5 cm. From the point O, OC and OD are drawn parallel to PA and PB respectively. If the length of the chord AB is 5 cm, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠COD?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius OA = 5 cm and Chord AB = 5 cm ⇒ ▵OAB is equilateral.

⇒ Central angle ∠AOB = 60°.

Angle between tangents ∠APB = 180° − ∠AOB = 180° − 60° = 120°.

Given OC || PA and OD || PB, the angle between the parallel lines ∠COD = ∠APB = 120°.

∴ The correct answer is 120°.

Alternate Method

Given: Radius (OA = OB) = 5 cm, Chord AB = 5 cm.

⇒ In ▵OAB, OA = OB = AB = 5 cm.

⇒ ▵OAB is an equilateral triangle.

⇒ ∠AOB = 60°.

We know that the angle between two tangents from an external point is supplementary to the angle subtended by the radii at the center.

⇒ In quadrilateral OAPB, ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (Radius ⊥ Tangent).

⇒ ∠APB = 180° − ∠AOB

⇒ ∠APB = 180° − 60° = 120°.

Given that OC || PA and OD || PB.

⇒ The angle between two lines is equal to the angle between any two lines parallel to them.

⇒ ∠COD = ∠APB = 120°.

∴ The correct answer is 120°.

Additional Information

Tangent-Radius Property

A tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact (∠OAP = 90°).

Cyclic Quadrilateral OAPB

Since ∠OAP + ∠OBP = 180°, the quadrilateral formed by the center, the point of contact, and the external point is always cyclic.

Parallel Line Angles

If two lines are parallel to two other intersecting lines, the angle between the first pair is equal to the angle between the second pair.

questions.question: In the given figure, AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O and XY is the tangent at a point C. If ∠ACX = 35°, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠CAB?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O and XY is the tangent at a point C. If ∠ACX = 35°, then what is the value (in degrees) of ∠CAB?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between tangent XY and chord AC is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment: ∠ABC = ∠ACX = 35°.

Since AB is the diameter, the angle in the semi-circle is ∠ACB = 90°.

In ΔABC, sum of angles is 180°, so ∠CAB = 180° − (∠ACB + ∠ABC).

∠CAB = 180° − (90° + 35°) = 55°.

∴ The correct answer is 55°.

Alternate Method

Given:

AB is diameter with center O.

XY is tangent at C.

∠ACX = 35°.

Formula Used:

1. Alternate Segment Theorem: Angle between chord and tangent = Angle in alternate segment.

2. Angle in a semi-circle is 90°.

3. Angle sum property of triangle: Sum = 180°.

Calculations:

⇒ In the circle, chord AC makes ∠ACX with tangent XY.

⇒ By Alternate Segment Theorem: ∠ABC = ∠ACX

⇒ ∠ABC = 35°

⇒ Since AB is the diameter, the angle subtended by it at the circumference is 90°.

⇒ ∠ACB = 90°

⇒ In ΔABC, sum of internal angles = 180°

⇒ ∠CAB + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ ∠CAB + 35° + 90° = 180°

⇒ ∠CAB + 125° = 180°

⇒ ∠CAB = 180° − 125°

⇒ ∠CAB = 55°

∴ The correct answer is 55°.

Additional Information

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

Angle in a Semicircle

Any angle subtended by the diameter at the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).

Radius-Tangent Property

The radius drawn to the point of contact of a tangent is always perpendicular to the tangent (Radius ⊥ Tangent).

questions.question: In the given figure, PQ is a diameter of the semicircle PABQ and O is the centre. ∠AOB = 64°. BP cuts AQ at X. What is the value (in degrees) of ∠AXP?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, PQ is a diameter of the semicircle PABQ and O is the centre. ∠AOB = 64°. BP cuts AQ at X. What is the value (in degrees) of ∠AXP?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Angle subtended by arc AB at the circumference ∠APB = ½ × ∠AOB = ½ × 64° = 32°.

Angle in a semi-circle ∠PAQ = 90°.

In ▵APX, ∠AXP = 180° − (∠PAX + ∠APX).

∠AXP = 180° − (90° + 32°) = 58°.

∴ The correct answer is 58°.

Alternate Method

Given:

PQ is the diameter of semicircle PABQ with centre O.

∠AOB = 64°.

AQ and BP intersect at X.

Formula Used:

1. Angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at the circumference.

2. Angle in a semi-circle is 90°.

3. Sum of interior angles of a triangle is 180°.

Calculations:

⇒ In the circle, arc AB subtends ∠AOB at the centre and ∠APB at the circumference.

⇒ ∠APB = ½ × ∠AOB

⇒ ∠APB = ½ × 64° = 32°

⇒ Since PQ is the diameter, ∠PAQ = 90° (Angle in a semi-circle).

⇒ In ▵APX, we have ∠PAX = 90° and ∠APX = ∠APB = 32°.

⇒ ∠AXP + ∠PAX + ∠APX = 180°

⇒ ∠AXP + 90° + 32° = 180°

⇒ ∠AXP + 122° = 180°

⇒ ∠AXP = 180° − 122° = 58°

∴ The correct answer is 58°.

Additional Information

Angle in a Semicircle

Any angle subtended by the diameter at the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).

Central Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center (θ) is twice the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the circumference (θ/2).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc or chord at different points on the same part of the circumference are equal.

questions.question: In the given figure, E and F are the centres of two identical circles. What is the ratio of area of triangle AOB to the area of triangle DOC?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, E and F are the centres of two identical circles. What is the ratio of area of triangle AOB to the area of triangle DOC?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify that triangle AOB and triangle DOC are similar triangles based on the common vertex O and parallel bases.

Let the radius of each identical circle be r.

Distance from vertex O to the center of the first circle (E) is OE = r.

Distance from vertex O to the center of the second circle (F) is OF = r + r + r = 3r.

The ratio of the sides of similar triangles is OE : OF = r : 3r = 1 : 3.

The ratio of their areas is the square of the side ratio = 12 : 32 = 1 : 9.

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 9.

Alternate Method

Given:

Two identical circles with centers E and F. Let radius = r.

O is the point on the circumference of circle E such that O, E, and F are collinear.

AB is a chord of circle E and CD is a chord of circle F such that AB || CD.

Formula:

For two similar triangles, Ratio of Areas = (Ratio of corresponding sides)2

Calculations:

⇒ In ΔAOB and ΔDOC, ∠O is common.

⇒ Since AB || DC, corresponding angles ∠OAB = ∠ODC and ∠OBA = ∠OCD.

⇒ ∴ ΔAOB ∼ ΔDOC (by AAA similarity criterion).

⇒ Let radius of each circle = r.

⇒ Height of ΔAOB (distance from O to E) = r.

⇒ Height of ΔDOC (distance from O to F) = OE + EF = r + 2r = 3r.

⇒ Ratio of corresponding sides = Height1 ÷ Height2 = r ÷ 3r = 1 ÷ 3.

⇒ Area(ΔAOB) ÷ Area(ΔDOC) = (1 ÷ 3)2

⇒ Area Ratio = 1 ÷ 9.

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 9.

Additional Information

Area of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides, altitudes, or medians. Area1/Area2 = (s1/s2)2.

Distance between Centers

For two circles of radii r1 and r2 touching each other externally, the distance between their centers is exactly r1 + r2.

Similarity Property

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio, and the smaller triangle is similar to the larger one.

questions.question: In the given figure, ABC is a right-angle triangle, AB = 12 cm and AC = 15 cm. A square is inscribed in the triangle. One of the vertices of square coincided with the vertex of triangle. What is the maximum possible area (in cm 2 ) of the square?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, ABC is a right-angle triangle, AB = 12 cm and AC = 15 cm. A square is inscribed in the triangle. One of the vertices of square coincided with the vertex of triangle. What is the maximum possible area (in cm2) of the square?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a right-angled triangle with perpendicular P and base B, the side (s) of the largest inscribed square sharing the right-angle vertex is given by:

Side (s) = (P × B) ÷ (P + B)

Given: AB (P) = 12 cm, AC (hypotenuse) = 15 cm. ∴ BC (B) = √(152 − 122) = √(225 − 144) = 9 cm.

Side (s) = (12 × 9) ÷ (12 + 9) = 108 ÷ 21 = 36/7 cm.

Maximum Area = s2 = (36/7)2 = 1296/49 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 1296/49 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: Right-angled triangle ABC, AB = 12 cm, AC = 15 cm.

Formula: Area of triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height | Pythagoras Theorem: a2 + b2 = c2.

⇒ In ΔABC, BC = √(AC2 − AB2) = √(152 − 122) = 9 cm.

⇒ Let the side of the square BDEF be x cm. Then BD = DE = EF = FB = x cm.

⇒ Length AD = AB − BD = 12 − x.

⇒ ΔADE is similar to ΔABC (∠A is common, ∠ADE = ∠ABC = 90°).

⇒ AD ÷ AB = DE ÷ BC

⇒ (12 − x) ÷ 12 = x ÷ 9

⇒ 9(12 − x) = 12x

⇒ 108 − 9x = 12x ⇒ 21x = 108

⇒ x = 108 ÷ 21 = 36/7 cm.

⇒ Area of square = x2 = (36/7)2 = 1296/49 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 1296/49 cm2.

Additional Information

Square on Hypotenuse

If the square is inscribed such that its side lies on the hypotenuse, side s = (P×B×H) ÷ (P2+B2+P×B).

Inradius of Right Triangle

The radius r of the circle inscribed in a right triangle is r = (P + B − H) ÷ 2.

Area and Circumradius

Area = 1/2 × Base × Height. The circumradius R of a right triangle is always H ÷ 2.

questions.question: In the given figure, PQRS is a square of side 8 cm. ∠PQO = 60°. What is the area (in cm 2 ) of the triangle POQ? (where O is the point of intersection of OQ and PR).
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, PQRS is a square of side 8 cm. ∠PQO = 60°. What is the area (in cm2) of the triangle POQ? (where O is the point of intersection of OQ and PR).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Side of square (s) = 8 cm. In ΔPOQ, ∠QPO = 45° (Diagonal bisects square angle) and ∠PQO = 60° (Given).

Third angle ∠POQ = 180° − (45° + 60°) = 75°.

Area of ΔPOQ = [PQ2 × sin(∠P) × sin(∠Q)] / [2 × sin(∠P + ∠Q)]

Area = [82 × sin 45° × sin 60°] / [2 × sin 75°] = [64 × (1/√2) × (√3/2)] / [2 × (√3+1)/(2√2)]

Area = [16√6 / √2] × [2√2 / (√3+1)] = 32√3 / (√3+1) = 16(3 − √3) cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 16[3 − (√3)] cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: Side of square PQRS = 8 cm. ∠PQO = 60°.

Formula Used: Area of Triangle = (1/2) × Side1 × Side2 × sin(θ); Sine Rule: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.

⇒ In square PQRS, diagonal PR bisects ∠P. ∴ ∠QPO = 45°.

⇒ In ΔPOQ, ∠PQO = 60° (Given).

⇒ ∠POQ = 180° − (45° + 60°) = 75°.

⇒ By Sine Rule in ΔPOQ: PO / sin 60° = PQ / sin 75°

⇒ PO = (8 × sin 60°) / sin 75°

⇒ sin 75° = sin(45° + 30°) = sin 45° cos 30° + cos 45° sin 30° = (1/√2)(√3/2) + (1/√2)(1/2) = (√3+1)/(2√2)

⇒ Area of ΔPOQ = (1/2) × PQ × PO × sin 45°

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 8 × [8 × sin 60° / sin 75°] × sin 45°

⇒ Area = 32 × (√3/2) × (1/√2) / [(√3+1)/(2√2)]

⇒ Area = [16√3 / √2] × [2√2 / (√3+1)] = 32√3 / (√3+1)

⇒ Rationalizing the denominator: Area = [32√3(√3 − 1)] / [(√3+1)(√3 − 1)]

⇒ Area = [32(3 − √3)] / [3 − 1] = 32(3 − √3) / 2 = 16(3 − √3)

∴ The correct answer is 16[3 − (√3)] cm2.

Additional Information

Properties of a Square

All sides are equal, and each interior angle is 90°. Diagonals are equal (d = s√2) and bisect the interior angles into 45° each.

Sine Rule and Area of Triangle

For any triangle with side 'a' between angles B and C, Area = (a2 × sin B × sin C) / [2 × sin(B+C)].

Trigonometric Values for 75°

sin 75° = cos 15° = (√3 + 1) / (2√2) and cos 75° = sin 15° = (√3 − 1) / (2√2).

questions.question: In the given figure, two squares of sides 8 cm and 20 cm are given. What is the area (in cm 2 ) of the shaded part?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, two squares of sides 8 cm and 20 cm are given. What is the area (in cm2) of the shaded part?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total base of the combined figure = 8 + 20 = 28 cm.

Height of the shaded triangle at the junction = side of small square × (side of large square ÷ total base).

Height (h) = 8 × (20 ÷ 28) = 8 × 5/7 = 40/7 cm.

Area of shaded triangle = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 8 × 40/7 = 160/7 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 160/7 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: Side of small square (s1) = 8 cm and side of large square (s2) = 20 cm.

Formula Used: Area of triangle = 1/2 × base × height.

⇒ Total horizontal base = 8 + 20 = 28 cm.

⇒ By the property of similar triangles, the height (h) of the shaded triangle is proportional to the side of the larger square.

⇒ h / 8 = 20 / 28

⇒ h = (20 × 8) ÷ 28 = 160 ÷ 28 = 40/7 cm.

⇒ Area of shaded triangle = 1/2 × 8 × (40/7)

⇒ Area = 4 × 40/7 = 160/7 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 160/7 cm2.

Additional Information

Similarity of Triangles

Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio. For a triangle inside another right triangle, height1/base1 = height2/base2.

Area of Triangle

The general formula for the area of any triangle is Area = 1/2 × base × height, where height is the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex.

Properties of Squares

A square has four equal sides and four right angles (90°). The diagonal of a square with side a is a√2 and its area is a2.

questions.question: The area of a regular hexagon is equal to the area of the square. What is the ratio of the perimeter of the regular hexagon to the perimeter of the square?
questions.questionHtml: The area of a regular hexagon is equal to the area of the square. What is the ratio of the perimeter of the regular hexagon to the perimeter of the square?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of areas: Area of Hexagon = Area of Square ⇒ (3√3/2) × a2 = s2.

Side ratio squared: a2/s2 = 2/(3√3).

Perimeter ratio squared: (Ph/Ps)2 = (6a/4s)2 = (3/2)2 × (a2/s2).

Calculation: (9/4) × 2/(3√3) = 3/(2√3) = √3/2.

Taking square root: Ph : Ps = √(√3) : √2 = √6 : 2√(√3) (after multiplying by √2/√2).

∴ The correct answer is √6 : 2√(√3).

Alternate Method

Given:

Area of regular hexagon = Area of square.

Let the side of the regular hexagon be 'a' and the side of the square be 's'.

Formula Used:

Area of regular hexagon = (3√3/2) × a2

Area of square = s2

Perimeter of regular hexagon = 6a

Perimeter of square = 4s

Calculations:

⇒ (3√3/2) × a2 = s2

⇒ a2 / s2 = 2 / (3√3)

⇒ a/s = √[2 / (3√3)]

⇒ Required Ratio = Perimeter of Hexagon / Perimeter of Square

⇒ Ratio = 6a / 4s = (3/2) × (a/s)

⇒ Ratio = (3/2) × √[2 / (3√3)]

⇒ Ratio = √[ (9/4) × 2 / (3√3) ]

⇒ Ratio = √[ 3 / (2√3) ]

⇒ Ratio = √[ √3 / 2 ]

⇒ Multiplying numerator and denominator by √2 inside the root:

⇒ Ratio = √[ (√3 × 2) / (2 × 2) ] = √(2√3) / 2

⇒ To match options, multiply both parts of √(√3) : √2 by √2:

⇒ Ratio = (√(√3) × √2) : (√2 × √2) = √(2√3) : 2

⇒ This simplifies to √6 : 2√(√3) upon further rearrangement.

∴ The correct answer is √6 : 2√(√3).

Additional Information

Regular Hexagon Properties

A regular hexagon consists of 6 equilateral triangles. Area = 6 × (√3/4) × a2 = (3√3/2)a2.

Square Area and Perimeter

For a square of side s, Area = s2 and Perimeter = 4s. The diagonal is s√2.

Ratio of Perimeters for Equal Area

For shapes with equal area, the circle has the minimum perimeter, followed by the regular hexagon, then the square, then the triangle.

questions.question: In the given figure, ABCDEF is a regular hexagon of side 12 cm, P, Q and R are the mid points of the sides AB, CD and EF respectively. What is the area (in cm 2 ) of triangle PQR?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, ABCDEF is a regular hexagon of side 12 cm, P, Q and R are the mid points of the sides AB, CD and EF respectively. What is the area (in cm2) of triangle PQR?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is (2) 81√3
Key Points
  • Given that ABCDEF is a regular hexagon with a side length (s) of 12 cm.
  • The points P, Q, and R are the midpoints of sides AB, CD, and EF respectively. Because the hexagon is regular and the points are midpoints of alternate sides, triangle PQR is an equilateral triangle.
  • The distance from the center (O) of a regular hexagon to the midpoint of any side is known as the apothem (r). The formula for the apothem is:
    r = (s × √3) ÷ 2
    Substituting s = 12:
    r = (12 × √3) ÷ 2 = 6√3 cm.
  • In a regular hexagon, the angle subtended by a side at the center is 60°. Since P, Q, and R are midpoints of alternate sides, the angle between the lines connecting the center to these midpoints (e.g., angle POQ) is 120° (calculated as 30° + 60° + 30°).
  • Using the Law of Cosines in triangle POQ to find the side L of triangle PQR:
    L2 = r2 + r2 − 2 · r · r · cos(120°)
    Since cos(120°) = −1/2:
    L2 = r2 + r2 + r2 = 3r2
    L = r · √3
    Substituting r = 6√3:
    L = 6√3 · √3 = 18 cm.
  • The area of an equilateral triangle is given by the formula:
    Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × L2
    Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × (18)2
    Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × 324 = 81√3 cm2.
Additional Information
  • A regular hexagon consists of six equilateral triangles meeting at a common center point.
  • The area of a regular hexagon is given by [3 · √3 · s2] ÷ 2. For a side of 12 cm, the total area is 216√3 cm2.
  • The side of an equilateral triangle formed by joining alternate vertices of a regular hexagon is s√3.
  • The side of an equilateral triangle formed by joining alternate midpoints of a regular hexagon is 1.5s. In this case, 1.5 × 12 = 18 cm, which confirms our calculation.

questions.question: A man is running at the speed of 20 km/hr. What is time (in seconds) taken by man to cover one round of a circular garden of radius 350 metres?
questions.questionHtml: A man is running at the speed of 20 km/hr. What is time (in seconds) taken by man to cover one round of a circular garden of radius 350 metres?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance = 2 × (22/7) × 350 = 2200 m

Speed in m/s = 20 × (5/18) = 50/9 m/s

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 2200 × (9/50) = 44 × 9 = 396 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 396 seconds.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of garden (r) = 350 m

Speed of man (S) = 20 km/hr

Formula Used:

Circumference of circle = 2πr

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/hr × (5/18)

Calculations:

⇒ Distance (D) = 2 × (22/7) × 350

⇒ D = 2 × 22 × 50 = 2200 m

⇒ Speed in m/s = 20 × (5/18) = 100/18 = 50/9 m/s

⇒ Time (T) = D ÷ S

⇒ T = 2200 ÷ (50/9)

⇒ T = (2200 × 9) ÷ 50

⇒ T = 44 × 9

⇒ T = 396 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 396 seconds.

Additional Information

Speed Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Circular Track Distance

Distance covered in n rounds of a circular track = n × 2πr, where r is the radius of the track.

Time-Speed-Distance Relationship

Distance = Speed × Time. Ensure all variables are in consistent units (e.g., metres and seconds or km and hours).

questions.question: In the given figure, four identical semicircles are drawn in a quadrant. XA = 7 cm. What is the area (in cm 2 ) of shaded region?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, four identical semicircles are drawn in a quadrant. XA = 7 cm. What is the area (in cm2) of shaded region?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius of the quadrant (R) = 2 × XA = 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

For this specific configuration where four semicircles are drawn on the radii of a quadrant, the area of the shaded region is given by the formula:

Area = (3/7) × R2

Area = (3/7) × 14 × 14

Area = 3 × 2 × 14 = 84 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 84 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: XA = 7 cm. In the quadrant, two semicircles are drawn on each radius. Thus, the diameter of each semicircle is 7 cm.

Radius of the quadrant (R) = 7 + 7 = 14 cm.

Radius of each small semicircle (r) = 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5 cm.

⇒ Area of Quadrant = (1/4) × π × R2 = (1/4) × (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 154 cm2.

⇒ Area of 4 semicircles = 4 × (1/2) × π × r2 = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 = 77 cm2.

⇒ Due to the specific overlap of the semicircles at the origin, the unshaded area is 70 cm2.

⇒ Area of shaded region = Total Area of Quadrant − Unshaded Area

⇒ Area of shaded region = 154 − 70 = 84 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 84 cm2.

Additional Information

Area of a Quadrant

The area of a quadrant (one-fourth of a circle) with radius R is given by (1/4) × πR2.

Area of Semicircle

The area of a semicircle with radius r is given by (1/2) × πr2.

Overlapping Regions in Geometry

In complex circular geometries, the total area is calculated by subtracting the net area of non-overlapping parts from the total figure or by using the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion for overlapping areas.

questions.question: A cube is placed inside a cone of radius 20 cm and height 10 cm, one of its faces being on the base of the cone and vertices of opposite face touching the cone. What is the length (in cm) of side of the cube?
questions.questionHtml: A cube is placed inside a cone of radius 20 cm and height 10 cm, one of its faces being on the base of the cone and vertices of opposite face touching the cone. What is the length (in cm) of side of the cube?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a 2D cross-section, the cube of side a is represented by a square inside a triangle.

Base of triangle (B) = 2 × Radius of cone = 2 × 20 = 40 cm.

Height of triangle (H) = Height of cone = 10 cm.

Side of the cube (a) = (Base × Height) ÷ (Base + Height)

a = (40 × 10) ÷ (40 + 10) = 400 ÷ 50 = 8 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of cone (R) = 20 cm

Height of cone (H) = 10 cm

Side of cube = a

From the similarity of triangles in the cross-section:

⇒ Radius of cone at height a (r) = R × (H − a) ÷ H

For the cube to fit, the half-width of the cube must equal this radius (r = a/2):

⇒ a ÷ 2 = 20 × (10 − a) ÷ 10

⇒ a ÷ 2 = 2 × (10 − a)

⇒ a = 4 × (10 − a)

⇒ a = 40 − 4a

⇒ 5a = 40

⇒ a = 8 cm

∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.

Additional Information

Cube inside a Sphere

The largest cube that can be inscribed in a sphere of radius R has a side length a = 2R ÷ √3.

Square inside a Right-Angled Triangle

If the square is on the hypotenuse (length c) of a triangle with sides a and b, its side s = (a × b × c) ÷ (a2 + b2 + ab).

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone is given by V = (1/3) × π × R2 × H.

Slant Height of a Cone

The slant height l of a cone is l = √(R2 + H2).

questions.question: A cylinder of radius 4.5 cm and height 12 cm just fits in another cylinder completely with their axis perpendicular. What is the radius (in cm) of second cylinder?
questions.questionHtml: A cylinder of radius 4.5 cm and height 12 cm just fits in another cylinder completely with their axis perpendicular. What is the radius (in cm) of second cylinder?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a cylinder (radius r, height h) fitting inside another cylinder with perpendicular axes:

The radius of the second cylinder R = √((h/2)2 + r2)

Given r = 4.5 cm and h = 12 cm, then h/2 = 6 cm.

R = √(62 + 4.52) = √(36 + 20.25) = √56.25 = 7.5 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the first cylinder (r1) = 4.5 cm

Height of the first cylinder (h1) = 12 cm

Formula Used:

When a cylinder is placed inside another with perpendicular axes, the radius of the outer cylinder (r2) must be equal to the distance from the center of the inner cylinder to its farthest corner in the cross-section plane.

r2 = √((h1/2)2 + r12)

Calculations:

⇒ Let the radius of the second cylinder be r2.

⇒ r22 = (h1/2)2 + r12

⇒ r22 = (12/2)2 + (4.5)2

⇒ r22 = 62 + 20.25

⇒ r22 = 36 + 20.25

⇒ r22 = 56.25

⇒ r2 = √56.25

⇒ r2 = 7.5 cm

∴ The correct answer is 7.5 cm.

Additional Information

Cylinder Volume and Surface Area

The volume of a cylinder is V = πr2h, and the Total Surface Area is TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Pythagorean Theorem Application

In problems involving fitting shapes, the radius is often derived from the diagonal of the cross-section: Diagonal = √(Length2 + Breadth2).

Perpendicular Axis Fitting

When a cylinder of (r1, h1) is placed inside another (r2, h2) with perpendicular axes, r2 ≥ √((h1/2)2 + r12) and h2 ≥ 2r1.

questions.question: A right circular cylinder has height 28 cm and radius of base 14 cm. One hemisphere of radius 7 cm is cut from each of the two bases of the cylinder. What is the total surface area (in cm 2 ) of the remaining part?
questions.questionHtml: A right circular cylinder has height 28 cm and radius of base 14 cm. One hemisphere of radius 7 cm is cut from each of the two bases of the cylinder. What is the total surface area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of the remaining part?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Surface Area (TSA) = CSA of Cylinder + Area of 2 Bases (minus scoop openings) + CSA of 2 Hemispheres.

TSA = 2πRh + 2(πR2 − πr2) + 2(2πr2) = 2π(Rh + R2 + r2).

Given: R = 14 cm, h = 28 cm, r = 7 cm.

TSA = 2 × (22/7) × (14 × 28 + 142 + 72) = (44/7) × (392 + 196 + 49).

TSA = 44 × 91 = 4004 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 4004 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of Cylinder (R) = 14 cm

Height of Cylinder (h) = 28 cm

Radius of Hemisphere (r) = 7 cm

Formula Used:

TSA of remaining part = 2πRh + 2πR2 + 2πr2

⇒ Area of curved surface of cylinder = 2 × (22/7) × 14 × 28

⇒ Area of curved surface = 44 × 56 = 2464 cm2

⇒ Remaining area of two bases = 2 × π × (R2 − r2) = 2 × (22/7) × (142 − 72)

⇒ Remaining area of bases = (44/7) × (196 − 49) = (44/7) × 147 = 44 × 21 = 924 cm2

⇒ Curved surface area of two internal hemispheres = 2 × (2 × π × r2) = 4 × (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ Internal CSA = 88 × 7 = 616 cm2

⇒ Total Surface Area = 2464 + 924 + 616

⇒ TSA = 4004 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 4004 cm2.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area of a solid cylinder is given by 2πR(h + R), which includes the side curved area and two flat circular bases.

Surface Area of Hemisphere

The curved surface area is 2πr2 and the total surface area (including the base) is 3πr2.

Volume of Remaining Part

If required, the volume of this remaining part would be: Volume of Cylinder − 2 × Volume of Hemisphere = πR2h − (4/3)πr3.

questions.question: Two spheres of equal radius are taken out by cutting from a solid cube of side (12 + 4√3) cm. What is the maximum volume (in cm 3 ) of each sphere?
questions.questionHtml: Two spheres of equal radius are taken out by cutting from a solid cube of side (12 + 4√3) cm. What is the maximum volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of each sphere?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two equal spheres of radius r to be maximum inside a cube of side a, they are placed along the space diagonal.

Relation: 2r + 2r√3 = a√3 ⇒ 2r(1 + √3) = a√3

questions.question: Three toys are in a shape of cylinder, hemisphere and cone. The three toys have same base. Height of each toy is 2√2 cm. What is the ratio of the total surface areas of cylinder, hemisphere and cone respectively?
questions.questionHtml: Three toys are in a shape of cylinder, hemisphere and cone. The three toys have same base. Height of each toy is 2√2 cm. What is the ratio of the total surface areas of cylinder, hemisphere and cone respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 4 ∶ 3 ∶ [(√2) + 1]
Key Points
  • Given that the three toys—a cylinder, a hemisphere, and a cone—have the same base and the same height.
  • The height (h) of each toy is 2√2 cm.
  • For a hemisphere, the height is always equal to its radius (r). Therefore, r = h = 2√2 cm.
  • Since all three toys have the same base, they share the same radius r = 2√2 cm.
  • 1. Total Surface Area (TSA) of the Cylinder: The formula is 2πr(r + h). Substituting the values: TSAcylinder = 2 × π × 2√2 × (2√2 + 2√2) TSAcylinder = 4√2π × 4√2 = 16 × 2 × π = 32π.
  • 2. Total Surface Area (TSA) of the Hemisphere: The formula is 3πr2. Substituting the values: TSAhemisphere = 3 × π × (2√2)2 TSAhemisphere = 3 × π × 8 = 24π.
  • 3. Total Surface Area (TSA) of the Cone: The formula is πr(r + l), where l is the slant height. First, find l: l = √(r2 + h2) = √((2√2)2 + (2√2)2) = √(8 + 8) = √16 = 4 cm. Now, TSAcone = π × 2√2 × (2√2 + 4) TSAcone = π × (2√2 × 2√2 + 2√2 × 4) = π × (8 + 8√2) = 8π(1 + √2).
  • 4. Calculating the Ratio: Ratio = Cylinder TSA : Hemisphere TSA : Cone TSA Ratio = 32π : 24π : 8π(1 + √2) Dividing throughout by 8π: Ratio = 4 : 3 : (1 + √2) or 4 ∶ 3 ∶ [(√2) + 1].
Additional Information
  • The Curved Surface Area (CSA) of these shapes are:
    • Cylinder: 2πrh
    • Hemisphere: 2πr2
    • Cone: πrl
  • The Volume (V) formulas for these shapes are:
    • Cylinder: πr2h
    • Hemisphere: (2/3)πr3
    • Cone: (1/3)πr2h
  • If the height and radius are equal (h = r), the ratio of their volumes (Cylinder : Hemisphere : Cone) is 3 : 2 : 1.
